study.title: Automated assessment of right ventricular systolic function from coronary angiograms with video-based artificial intelligence algorithms: development, validation, comparison against humans, and prospective deployment

imaging.modality_detail: Routine invasive coronary angiogram videos (DICOM), left and right coronary artery videos, 7 or 15 frames per second
imaging.territory_detail: Left and right coronary angiograms used to predict right ventricular systolic function
imaging.frames_per_sequence: minimum of 7 frames; acquired at 7 or 15 frames per second

public_dataset_used.detail: Only Kinetics400 used for pretraining weights; study data are private MHI and UCSF angiograms

data_released.detail: Datasets not publicly available due to patient privacy; may be available on reasonable request

annotation.annotator_expertise: Labels derived from clinical transthoracic echocardiography (TAPSE, FAC, visual assessment)

task.task_description: Video-based deep neural network (DeepRV) classifying right ventricular systolic function as normal or reduced (echocardiography reference) from routine left and right coronary angiogram videos, aggregated to study level; internal test, external validation at UCSF, prospective deployment in STEMI, and reader study with/without AI.
task.clinical_application: Point-of-care rule-out of right ventricular dysfunction during coronary angiography/primary PCI without additional imaging

temporal_evidence.quote: Multi-view coronary angiogram videos from left and right coronary arteries are processed through a video-based spatiotemporal deep neural network.

evaluation.external_validation_detail: External validation at UCSF (2247 studies, 2031 patients, 2012-2019); prospective deployment via PACS-AI in 82 consecutive STEMI cases at MHI (January-June 2025)

G2.quote: To assess the generalizability of DeepRV, we conducted an external validation study using coronary angiograms from the University of California of San Francisco (UCSF).

G3.quote: activation intensifying as coronary arteries opacified, suggesting temporal awareness of contrast dynamics

G5.quote: lack of core lab assessment of RVSF and potential inter-observer variability in TTE interpretation

G6.quote: We conducted a prospective evaluation of the model by applying DeepRV by the interventional cardiologist on consecutive STEMI patients between January 2025 and June 2025

G7.quote: To interpret our DeepRV algorithm's decision-making process, we employed two complementary explainability techniques

G8.quote: Future work could look at integrating ECG with DeepRV to improve model performance

G9.quote: small sample sizes for critical subgroups (cardiogenic shock n = 4, reduced PAPi n = 31)

other_limitations: No race/ethnicity data, preventing fairness/bias assessment
Reference standard limited to echocardiography (no cardiac MRI/RHC validation)
Temporal mismatch between angiography and TTE (up to 5 days)
Poor performance in RCA-culprit STEMI on diagnostic-phase angiograms
future_work: Dedicated validation in isolated RV infarction and cardiogenic shock
External validation and fine-tuning using released open weights
Automated biventricular assessment combining DeepRV and CathEF
